title: Corby metal pollution may harm people, says Earthwatch Europe
summary:
Campaigners trying to examine the effects of the toxic waste scandal in Corby say they have found a presence of metals that could pose a risk to human health.
Children in the Northamptonshire town have been born with birth defects, believed to have been caused when steelworks were demolished in the 1980s.
Charity Earthwatch Europe says trained citizen scientists have found potentially harmful levels of metal or metalloid at 52 freshwater sites across Corby.
The Environment Agency (EA) welcomed their work but said some metals occurred naturally and that its own evidence did not indicate "widespread or significant harm".
Earlier this year, Earthwatch Europe said its volunteers collected evidence that the presence of metals could harm aquatic life - findings that were disputed by the EA.

title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
summary:
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.
Left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon.
Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.
The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.
The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

title: Climate scientists face deluge of public-records requests about fossil-fuel studies
summary:
An investigation by Nature has identified at least 30 requests for correspondence relating to climate attribution science that researchers in the United States say they have received since 2024.
These requests, involving the Patriots Foundation and other groups, have gone to 13 public universities and involved the correspondence of dozens of climate scientists, legal scholars and attorneys.
But some say that the volume of requests seems intended to dissuade work on climate attribution, and wastes time and public money.
“Climate attribution is under attack,” says Christopher Callahan, a climate scientist at Indiana University Bloomington.
‘It’s totally a surge’The volume of requests for climate researchers has noticeably increased this year, says Lauren Kurtz at the Climate Science Legal Defense Fund in New York City, an organization that helps scientists to address legal issues in this field.

title: BBC visits Indonesia's wildfire ground blanketed by toxic haze
summary:
As Indonesia battles its worst wildfire season in a decade, a toxic haze is choking millions of residents in the region.
The BBC's Liza Tambunan is in central Kalimantan, where air pollution levels have plunged to hazardous levels.
The haze has been linked to hundreds of thousands of respiratory illnesses in Indonesia, and has drifted to neighbouring countries like Singapore and Malaysia.

title: Search continues after boat capsizes off Baja California coast. Survivors attacked by sharks
summary:
